items.title: Oracle-bone decipherment award: 100,000 yuan per new reading, 50,000 yuan per disputed graph
items.who: National Museum of Chinese Writing, Anyang
items.note: Open call for readings of unread graphs, each submission backed by two senior referees and judged by an expert committee convened through the national social-science planning office.

items.title: Decipherment of oracle-bone graphs supported by big data and cloud platforms
items.who: Li Xueqin (chief expert) and ten sub-projects
items.venue: National Social Science Fund of China, major commissioned project
items.note: National project begun in late October 2016 linking CASS, Tsinghua, Peking and Fudan universities to build full-text and image databases of the inscriptions.

items.title: Yinqi Wenyuan 殷契文渊 oracle-bone big-data platform opened to the public
items.who: Anyang Normal University
items.note: Combined graph, catalogue and literature databases; by 2024 it reported 153 published catalogues, about 239,000 images and over 33,000 studies.

items.title: The Oracle Bone Inscriptions from Huayuanzhuang East
items.who: A. C. Schwartz
items.note: Annotated English translation of the non-royal inscriptions excavated in 1991, a complete, provenanced group for testing readings in context.

items.title: Joining jades and linking pearls: 120 Years of rejoining fragmented oracle bone inscriptions
items.who: Jiang Yubin
items.note: Survey of a century of fragment joins, the work that restores the context on which readings of rare graphs depend.

items.title: First awards: 100,000 yuan to Jiang Yubin, 50,000 yuan to Wang Ziyang
items.who: National Museum of Chinese Writing, Anyang
items.note: The first batch, announced at the end of 2022, six years after the call: one first-class award (Fudan) and one second-class award (Tsinghua).

items.title: Jiaguwen moben daxi 甲骨文摹本大系
items.who: Huang Tianshu (chief ed.), Tsinghua University
items.note: Forty-three-volume facsimile corpus of 70,659 inscribed pieces, deduplicated, with joins to 2020 and each piece assigned to a script group.

items.title: Second awards: two first-class (Chen Jian, Zhou Zhongbing) and three second-class prizes
items.who: National Museum of Chinese Writing, Anyang
items.note: Announced at the end of 2023; Chen Jian's winning paper identifies a variant of 徹 from differences between diviner groups, and the others go to Wang Ziyang, Xie Mingwen and Li Chuntao.

items.title: The "graphic design" for 旅 'troops' and 車 'chariot' in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions
items.who: C. Maréchal and K. Takashima
items.note: Traces how two graphs were composed and changed from oracle-bone to bronze inscriptions, the kind of form-tracing that decipherment arguments depend on.

items.title: An open dataset for the evolution of oracle bone characters: EVOBC
items.who: H. Guan, J. Wan, Y. Liu et al.
items.note: Image dataset linking graphs across six stages from oracle-bone to later scripts, intended for machine tracing of forms forward through time.

items.title: Deciphering Oracle Bone Language with Diffusion Models
items.who: H. Guan, H. Yang, X. Wang et al.
items.note: Conditional diffusion model that generates candidate modern forms as decipherment clues; won an ACL 2024 Best Paper award, though tested on known graphs.

items.title: International conference marking 125 years since the discovery of the oracle-bone inscriptions
items.who: Oracle-bone specialists convened in Jinan
items.note: Papers on new readings drew on joins, scraping, partial graphs and carving technique; the report puts the inventory at nearly 4,400 graphs, about 1,700 read.

items.title: An open dataset for oracle bone character recognition and decipherment (HUST-OBC)
items.who: P. Wang, K. Zhang, X. Wang et al.
items.note: Openly released 140,053 images of 1,588 deciphered and 9,411 undeciphered graph categories; the common benchmark for later AI work.

items.title: OBI-Bench: Can LMMs Aid in Study of Ancient Script on Oracle Bones?
items.who: Z. Chen, T. Chen, W. Zhang et al.
items.note: Benchmark of 5,523 images on recognition, rejoining, classification, retrieval and decipherment; general multimodal models performed far below experts.

items.title: AI-assisted oracle-bone research invitational competition
items.who: Henan Provincial Administration of Cultural Heritage, Anyang government, Anyang Normal University and Tencent SSV
items.venue: China (Anyang) International Conference of Chinese Characters
items.note: Research, algorithm (fragment joining and duplicate-rubbing detection) and creative tracks; 22 decipherment teams entered and 8 were shortlisted by October 2025.

items.title: InteChar: A Unified Oracle Bone Character List for Ancient Chinese Language Modeling
items.who: X. Diao, Z. Zhou, L. Shi et al.
items.note: Character list encoding unencoded oracle-bone graphs alongside traditional and modern Chinese, with a corpus for training language models on the inscriptions.

items.title: Yinqi Xingzhi 殷契行止 oracle-bone agent
items.who: Anyang Normal University, Tencent SSV, Tencent Youtu Lab and Xiamen University
items.note: Free recognition, comparison and retrieval tool built on 1.43 million graph records; its makers report leads on more than ten unread graphs, not yet reviewed.

items.title: OracleAgent: A Multimodal Reasoning Agent for Oracle Bone Script Research
items.who: C. Li, Z. Ding, X. Hu et al.
items.note: LLM agent orchestrating oracle-bone analysis tools over an expert-annotated knowledge base of over 1.4 million single-graph rubbing images.

items.title: Oracle Bone Inscriptions: A New Exploration of the Three-Thousand-Year-Old Chinese Writing System
items.who: Chen Tingzhu
items.note: Study of variants, graph structure, components and character frequency across the corpus, offering quantitative baselines for judging new readings.

items.title: AlphaOracle: Oracle bone script decipherment via human-workflow-inspired deep learning
items.who: Y. Liu, H. Guan, P. Wang et al.
items.note: Pipeline producing evidence chains from form, context and classical texts; its readings agreed with experts on test graphs, and it proposes 'Lao' as a place or clan name.
